name: Saleph River
summary: The river in Cilicia traditionally associated with Frederick Barbarossa’s drowning in 1190.
overview: The Saleph River, often identified with the Goksu in Cilicia, is traditionally associated with the death of Frederick I Barbarossa during the Third Crusade.
His drowning in 1190 shocked the crusading army and weakened the German expedition.

contentSections.title: Overview
paragraphs: The Saleph (Göksu) River in Cilicia (modern southern Turkey) was the site where Frederick I Barbarossa, Holy Roman Emperor and leader of the German crusade army, drowned in June 1190 while crossing. His death was one of the most consequential events of the Third Crusade.

contentSections.title: Legacy
paragraphs: Frederick's drowning at the Saleph devastated the large German crusading force. Much of his army dispersed after his death; only a remnant continued to the Holy Land under his son Frederick of Swabia. The collapse of the German contingent left Richard I of England and Philip II of France as the dominant leaders of the Third Crusade and contributed to its failure to retake Jerusalem.
